description: Adversaries may backdoor web servers with web shells to establish persistent access to systems. A web shell is a web script that is placed on an openly accessible web server to allow an adversary to access the web server as a gateway into a network.
artifacts: HTTP POST requests with file upload containing PHP/script content
multipart/form-data requests uploading executable file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5)
HTTP requests to newly created files in upload directories
command execution patterns in HTTP parameters (cmd=, command=, c=)
HTTP responses containing OS command output (uid=, whoami, /etc/passwd)
suspicious user-agent strings or raw curl/python upload requests
outbound reverse shell connections following web shell access

pcaps.name: Web shell upload - p0wny-shell (curl)
pcaps.description: Unauthenticated upload of p0wny-shell (interactive PHP web shell) via the vulnerable file upload endpoint. No extension or MIME validation performed.

pcaps.name: Web shell upload - pentestmonkey reverse shell (curl)
pcaps.description: Unauthenticated upload of pentestmonkey PHP reverse shell via the vulnerable file upload endpoint. No extension or MIME validation performed.

pcaps.name: Web shell upload - weevely backdoor (curl)
pcaps.description: Unauthenticated upload of a weevely-generated PHP backdoor via the vulnerable file upload endpoint. No extension or MIME validation performed.

pcaps.name: Web shell execution - p0wny-shell interactive session
pcaps.description: Interactive command execution via p0wny-shell after successful upload. The web shell provides a browser-based terminal with AJAX requests for each command executed.

pcaps.name: Web shell execution - pentestmonkey reverse shell callback
pcaps.description: Triggering the pentestmonkey PHP reverse shell by accessing the uploaded file. The server initiates an outbound TCP connection back to the attacker's listener.

pcaps.name: Web shell execution - weevely C2 session
pcaps.description: Establishing a weevely C2 session by connecting to the uploaded backdoor. Weevely uses obfuscated HTTP requests to execute commands on the target.
